title: Three Years and One Short Plan
subtitle: 历史古迹 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 历史古迹（人与社会·历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）
meta: 主题语境：历史古迹（人与社会·历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）　|　核心词汇：monument　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 monument 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the planner ① built the monument that no citizen in the district would have measured, and he said the building was the whole of the year. The ② monument, meaning the stone itself and not the plan, ran three years and stayed unmeasured in the book; a monument, he said, is the only thing in a district that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ monument in that district had the same short plan beside it, and the ④ monument at the far square, meaning the plot they kept for the children to measure and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A monument, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the planner said the measuring is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the monument was the whole of the matter, meaning the memory and not the stone. The ⑥ monument, meaning the memory and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; monument, he said, is either something you build or the only word that means both a stone and a memory. He said the memory is the part they remember.

By 1984 the ⑦ monument had become a line in a report, and the report had become an argument about the short plan. The ⑧ monument of the whole thing, the planner wrote in March, was one district and three years of measuring; monument, he said, is either the plot at the far square or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ monument I remember is the stone measured in the report, which closed in 1986 and is still measured as the quietest in the district. A ⑩ monument, my mother said in 1988, is the only stone that improves by being measured; every monument, she said, is a memory that has agreed to look like a stone. She said the memory was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 纪念碑；遗迹（指街区里每一座旁边的那一座）
B. n. 纪念碑；遗迹（指那座纪念碑本身，与薄薄的图纸相对）
C. 固定搭配：build the monument 修建这一座纪念碑
D. n. 纪念碑；遗迹（指留给孩子们丈量的那一块）
E. n. 纪念碑之事（抽象总称，指一处街区的纪念碑之事）
F. n. 纪念碑；遗迹（指规划报告里写到、被测量的那一座）
G. n. 纪念碑、记忆（指一件事里人人都用却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 记忆（抽象总称，指人人都用却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: built the monument that no citizen in the district would have measured
The monument, meaning the stone itself and not the plan
the monument at the far square
the monument was the whole of the matter
the monument had become a line in a report
The monument of the whole thing
A monument, my mother said in 1988

answers.why: build the monument 意为“修建这一座纪念碑”，1979 年那位规划员把街区里没有一位市民肯测量的一座纪念碑做了一遍。
monument 意为“纪念碑；遗迹”，指那座纪念碑本身而不是薄薄的图纸，它经过了三个年份而在簿子上没有被测量。
monument 意为“纪念碑；遗迹”，指街区里每一座旁边的那一座，每一座旁边都有同一张薄薄的图纸。
monument 意为“纪念碑；遗迹”，指最远那处广场的留给孩子们丈量的那一块，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
monument 意为“纪念碑、记忆”，指一件事里人人都用却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这座记忆就是那件事的全部。
monument 意为“记忆”，指人人都用却无人提起的那样东西而不是那座纪念碑，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
monument 意为“纪念碑；遗迹”，指规划报告里写到、被测量的那一座，到 1984 年这一座成了规划报告里的一行。
monument 意为“纪念碑之事”，规划员三月写道，整件事的纪念碑之事是一处街区和三个年份的测量。
monument 意为“纪念碑；遗迹”，我记得的是规划报告里测量过的那一座，1986 年落成了，至今仍被说成街区里最安静的一座。
monument 为抽象总称，母亲 1988 年说，纪念碑是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的纪念碑。
